Chapter 10: Leading for the Long Haul—Legacy, Meaning, and the Future.
You know, at the end of the day, most of us want to feel like our work actually matters. We want to be part of something bigger, to leave a mark that lasts beyond our time. The best leaders? They get this. They aren’t just chasing the next quarter’s numbers or eyeing the next big promotion. Instead, they’re thinking about the legacy they’re building, the culture they’re shaping, and the lives they’re touching along the way.
There’s a story I love about a teacher who spent decades in the classroom. Someone once asked her what made her the most proud. She didn’t bring up any awards or special recognition. What really mattered to her were the students who came back years later just to say thank you. The ones who remembered a kind word, a moment of encouragement, or simply the feeling that they truly belonged. That, she said, was her real legacy.
The same thing holds true in any organization. Leaders who pour into their people, who build real trust and foster a sense of belonging, end up leaving much more than just profits or products behind. They create cultures where people thrive, where teams come together, and where the impact lasts long after they’re gone.
Most folks don’t realize just how much influence they have, every single day. Every decision, every quick conversation, every little choice—it all shapes the future. When leaders focus on meaning and legacy, they naturally inspire others to do the same. They remind everyone around them that work isn’t just about what you accomplish, but about who you become along the way.
Of course, it’s not always easy. There are setbacks, disappointments, and those tough moments of doubt. But the leaders who keep their eyes on the bigger picture—who put people first, even when it’s challenging—are the ones who build organizations that truly stand the test of time.
